% ---------- Figure A: DA distribution by turn ------------------------
\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{outputs/da_hist_gdpzero_vs_emomcts_40s.png}
\caption{System dialogue-act distribution by turn at $n_\text{sims}{=}40$ (PersuasionForGood,
Vicuna-13B). EmoMCTS sustains emotion appeals deeper into the dialogue and proposes donation
earlier and more steadily, whereas GDP-Zero front-loads credibility appeals and defers the
proposition.}
\label{fig:da-by-turn}
\end{figure}

% ---------- Figure B: emotion-conditioned action choice --------------
\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.92\linewidth]{outputs/emotion_conditioned_actions_40s.png}
\caption{Action choice conditioned on the user's last emotion ($n_\text{sims}{=}40$). Actions
are grouped into trust-building (\{emotion, credibility appeal\}), proposition, and other
(\{greeting, task inquiry, logical appeal\}); the preceding user emotion is bucketed as negative
(\{fear, sadness, anger, disgust, contempt\}) vs non-negative. After a \emph{negative} user
emotion EmoMCTS shifts toward trust-building (0.73 vs 0.60) and nearly eliminates off-topic
actions (0.07 vs 0.20), repairing affect before closing; after a non-negative emotion the two
planners behave almost identically. EmoMCTS logs emotions directly; GDP-Zero's user turns are
labelled with the same deterministic HF classifier. Negative-emotion buckets are small
($n{=}15$ per planner) and should be read as indicative.}
\label{fig:emotion-conditioned-actions}
\end{figure}
